headline: High: shared browser/MCP-capable document agent can feed untrusted content into a social uploader, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can run browsers and use MCP, so it may ingest untrusted document/web content. Agent B is a CLI social uploader with broad network egress and subagents, so if A’s output is passed into B without isolation, injected instructions could propagate. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF A’s browser-sourced content is copied into B’s prompts or account files
IF an MCP tool returns attacker-controlled text that B treats as instructions
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of raw web text between agents
Add a prompt firewall that strips instructions from A outputs
Run B only on pre-sanitized summaries
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to A outputs
requires-engineering: isolate A and B in separate workspaces

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A handles PDFs, text, images, and API keys, while Agent B handles account data and uploads media over broad egress. If A’s documents or secrets are forwarded into B’s upload workflow, sensitive content can leave the local workspace. The pair has no documented shared filesystem, so the leakage path is inferred and not proven.
conditions: IF A’s PDF/text/image outputs are placed into B’s upload inputs
IF A’s API key or other secrets are included in files B can transmit
mitigations: Review B inputs before upload
Keep secrets out of shared files
Use separate directories for A and B
requires-engineering: enforce file allowlists
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning before network egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A supports multiple instances and broad network egress; B also supports multiple instances and broad network egress, but B cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. The profiles do not show a shared mutable resource, so direct write-write conflict is not established. Uncertainty keeps this at low rather than none because overlapping networked actions could still contend externally.
conditions: IF both agents target the same external account or API quota
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable resource
mitigations: Stagger runs to avoid quota contention
Assign separate accounts
Use per-agent rate limits
requires-engineering: add resource locks
requires-engineering: partition shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A produces AI-assisted visualizations from documents, and Agent B is a social-media uploader that can act on prepared media. If B consumes A’s generated artifacts without verification, A’s mistakes can cascade into published content or account actions. B’s CLI/subagent workflow suggests action-taking authority, but no explicit verification step is documented.
conditions: IF B publishes or uploads artifacts generated by A without human review
IF A’s diagram/text extraction is used as authoritative source material
mitigations: Require human review before upload
Compare A outputs against source documents
Use a checklist for publish-ready assets
requires-engineering: add validation gates in B
requires-engineering: separate draft and publish stages

E_compliance.rationale: A handles API keys and document content; B handles account data and uploads to social platforms. The profiles show different data classes and broad network egress, but no residency or certification details, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because the pair could move sensitive document-derived content into a social uploader, the safer choice is medium under uncertainty.
conditions: IF document-derived personal data is uploaded through B
IF A’s secrets or account data are retained in B’s logs or account files
mitigations: Classify data before transfer
Avoid sending regulated data to B
Review retention settings
requires-engineering: document residency and DPA boundaries
requires-engineering: add deletion/export workflows
